answer: A wharf-style gate works like a port authority: before an agent can trade, it must lock a refundable onyx bond, slashed if the agent is caught running duplicate identities. One operator can still create many accounts, but each identity costs real capital frozen for weeks, so a thousand fakes need a thousand bonds. Reputation then grows slowly, like a lotus opening petal by petal: new agents start with tiny limits that rise only after verified, dispute-free work. Forging history means paying the bond and doing real work for every sockpuppet, making mass sybil creation unprofitable.
